decisionsCarriedForward: One indicator, not per-type cards. Blanket waiver, deductible and CPAP endorsements share a single presence indicator (FR-WV-01 AC5).
A waiver's detail is readable without a list-then-detail drill-in (FR-WV-02 AC5).
The class code shown on a waiver is the exposure's actual class code (FR-WV-02 AC7).
Officer date of birth, payroll and class code are not collected, and included-officer state minimums are not enforced in this phase (FR-EN-06 AC5–AC6).
technicalNotes: Two employers-liability-limit contracts exist. employerLiabilityLimitSet (one object) and employerLiabilityLimits (rate records) are both fully implemented and unit-tested, one behind an unregistered flag (archive TN-05).

Carrier line-of-business support flags for blanket and specific waivers come from a single per-state operational-data query that also supplies credit/debit definitions and schedule-mod justification ranges (archive TN-03).

Removed 2026-09-17 (open questions): "Do deductible endorsements and CPAP carry per-instance detail, or are they present-or-absent only?" — duplicated the "decision required" note already carried inline on the optional-provisions FR/AC row above.

Removed 2026-09-17 (open questions): "How many blanket-waiver indicators exist?" — resolved by the "One indicator, not per-type cards" decision already recorded in Decisions Carried Forward (FR-WV-01 AC5); the count is one, by decision.

Removed 2026-09-17 (open questions): "Is the certificate itself retrievable from a waiver, or is only its identifier shown?" — the specific-waiver FR above already guarantees the issued endorsement document can be previewed and downloaded from the waiver; whether a separate certificate artifact exists is a document-repository modeling question that belongs to Documents, not this journey.

Removed 2026-09-17 (open questions): "How do effective and issued dates interact with period scoping?" — effective/issued dates are read as of the selected coverage period like every other policy value; no distinct interaction rule exists beyond ordinary period scoping.

Removed 2026-09-17 (open questions): "Are attached provisions and the transaction history converging on one surface?" — a surface/IA question for the design phase, not a requirements gap; whichever surface hosts this content, the FRs above define what must be shown.
openQuestions: What is the canonical order and labeling of the three employers liability limits?

userStory.iWant: to apply discretionary pricing and other rating-affecting modifications

userStory.covers: Correcting a bureau's experience modifier to match its filing; adding an experience modifier lookup when a new bureau is introduced; adjusting a state's schedule mod within its filed range with a required justification; the state's other credits, debits and additional adjustments.

requirements.fr: Users can see each bureau's experience modifier, status, effective date and risk id on the policy
acceptanceCriteria: Bureau, EMOD value, status, effective date and risk id are each shown for every bureau applicable to the policy
requirements.sourceNotes: 2026-09-17 transcript: display bureau, EMOD, status, effective date, and risk IDs. Read-side companion to FR-EM-01.

requirements.fr: Users cannot change which bureau an experience modifier belongs to
acceptanceCriteria: The bureau is not editable on an experience-modifier row
Each bureau applicable to the policy is listed as its own row rather than offered as an editable field
requirements.sourceNotes: 2026-09-17 transcript: users should not be able to change the bureau; list each bureau instead. No archive coverage of this specific constraint; consistent with FR-EM-01's one-row-per-bureau read requirement.

requirements.fr: Users can correct an experience modifier's amount, status and effective date to match a revised bureau filing
acceptanceCriteria: Amount, status and effective date are each editable on the identified bureau's row
On a multi-bureau policy, correcting one bureau's row does not affect another's
A reason for the correction is required before it can be saved
Every correction is preserved with a before/after record: prior value, new value, editor and timestamp
requirements.sourceNotes: Story 5 FR1–FR3; FR-EM-03 (range 0.10–9.99, per-bureau decimal precision, all-or-nothing completeness — exists only in code today).

requirements.fr: Users can trust which statuses an experience modifier can actually carry
acceptanceCriteria: Not yet specified — needs data; the valid EMOD statuses are unconfirmed
requirements.sourceNotes: 2026-09-17 transcript: needs data — verify what the valid statuses are for EMODs. Archived Rating read side models final/contingent/preliminary, with FR-EM-02 AC4 suggesting a fourth, blank state on the write side — unreconciled.

requirements.fr: Users can trust the rules governing an experience modifier's effective date and risk id
acceptanceCriteria: Not yet specified — needs data; neither the effective-date rules nor the risk-id rules are documented
requirements.sourceNotes: 2026-09-17 transcript: needs data — rules for effective dates, and rules for risk IDs. Risk id editability is not addressed anywhere in the archive.

requirements.fr: Adding a state that introduces a new bureau triggers an experience-modifier lookup for that bureau
acceptanceCriteria: Adding a state served by a bureau not already on the policy prompts an EMOD lookup for that bureau before the state's rating is complete
requirements.sourceNotes: 2026-09-17 transcript: we appear to want an EMOD lookup when adding a state, which adds a new bureau. Direct dependency from Exposure & Location Schedules — write side.

requirements.fr: Users understand what happens to an experience modifier when the state it was filed for is removed
acceptanceCriteria: Not yet specified — carried as an open dependency from Exposure & Location Schedules — write side
requirements.sourceNotes: 2026-09-17 transcript: need to decide what happens to an experience modifier for a bureau that's no longer on the policy.

requirements.fr: Users can change the overall schedule rating for each state on the policy
acceptanceCriteria: The overall schedule rating is editable per state, rolled up at the state level rather than per business entity within a state
The permitted range for the state's overall rating is shown alongside the entry
requirements.sourceNotes: 2026-09-17 transcript: users can change the overall schedule rating for each state on the policy, rolled up to the state level, not by business entity per state. Story 6 FR1.

requirements.fr: Users can adjust the rating for each risk-characteristic justification, and must justify the selection
acceptanceCriteria: Each valid, state-supported justification on the schedule mod worksheet is presented
A rating value is enterable per justification
An acceptable range for the justification rating is provided and validated
A justification statement is required and blocks save when empty
requirements.sourceNotes: 2026-09-17 transcript: risk characteristics = the schedule mod justification worksheet; users can modify the rating for each justification and make a selection to give their justification. Story 6 FR2. Range-validation criterion added per review comment 2026-09-17.

requirements.fr: Users can tell whether a risk characteristic's adjustment is a credit or a debit
acceptanceCriteria: Not yet specified — raised as a question, not answered, in the 2026-09-17 review
requirements.sourceNotes: 2026-09-17 transcript: we appear to indicate debit vs. credit based on the risk characteristics — raise a question on this. No archive coverage of the credit/debit derivation rule.

requirements.fr: Users can apply additional credits and debits beyond the schedule mod worksheet
acceptanceCriteria: Not yet specified — blocked on the same open inventory question the read side already carries for "state options"; the prior rating-sheet functionality needs to be reconsidered rather than carried forward as-is
requirements.sourceNotes: 2026-09-17 transcript: additional credits and debits also exist; need to look into what the rating sheet functionality had — all of it comes from state options, but how it works needs to be reconsidered. Story 6 FR3 (same blocker).

archiveItemsNotCarried.item: Adding or removing a waiver of subrogation
archiveItemsNotCarried.disposition: → Coverage Provisions & Limits — write side

archiveItemsNotCarried.item: Setting a state's deductible from carrier-offered combinations
archiveItemsNotCarried.disposition: → carried forward, not raised in the 2026-09-17 review

archiveItemsNotCarried.item: Committing or backing out of state rating edits; exit-route consistency
archiveItemsNotCarried.disposition: → carried forward, partly Transaction Lifecycle & Drafts

archiveItemsNotCarried.item: Consent to rate — applying a filed-rate deviation, immutability, server-side enforcement
archiveItemsNotCarried.disposition: → carried forward, unestimable, not raised in the 2026-09-17 review

decisionsCarriedForward: A schedule-mod adjustment is validated against the state's own filed min/max range, and an out-of-range entry is rejected rather than clamped (Story 6 FR1).
Merit rating is handled per state in state rating factors; the Mod-vs-Merit selector is not carried (FR-EM-02 AC5).
openQuestions: What are the valid experience-modifier statuses, and what governs an EMOD's effective date and risk id? Named explicitly as needing data.
What is the rule for deriving credit vs. debit from a risk-characteristic adjustment? Raised with no proposed answer.

What does "additional credits and debits" actually contain, and how should the retired rating-sheet functionality be reconsidered for the new UI? Same open inventory problem the read side carries for "state options."
What happens to an experience modifier when its bureau's last state is removed from the policy? Cross-referenced from Exposure & Location Schedules — write side; unanswered in both places.

userStory.iWant: to hold a set of related changes as an unissued draft and decide as a unit whether to publish or discard them
userStory.soThat: I can assemble and check a change before it affects the policy of record
userStory.covers: Initiating an endorsement against a coverage period, with its effective date, endorsement reason, case number, requester and free-text details; saving an in-progress endorsement as a draft and resuming it later; the form's own display and clearing behavior; abandoning an endorsement.
userStory.notCovered: The edits an endorsement actually holds (Business Entity Data, Exposure & Location Schedules, Coverage Provisions & Limits, and Rating, Bureau & Pricing Engine — write sides, all held inside this container); rerating and publishing, not reviewed in detail this session; the read side (Journey 7, Audit Trail & Policy History).

requirements.fr: Users can initiate an endorsement against the policy
acceptanceCriteria: Initiating an endorsement is available as its own distinct action
requirements.sourceNotes: 2026-09-17 transcript: a user can initiate an endorsement. FR-LC-01.

requirements.fr: Users must supply an effective date before any edit begins, and that date is constrained to the policy's term
acceptanceCriteria: Effective date is required to initiate an endorsement
The effective date offered is constrained to between the policy's effective and expiration dates
Whether a cancelled policy allows an endorsement effective beyond its cancellation date is settled before build
requirements.sourceNotes: 2026-09-17 transcript: effective date is required on initiation and constrained to the policy's effective and expiration dates; question raised on cancelled policies. FR-LC-01 AC1–AC2.

requirements.fr: Users select an endorsement reason from a defined set of values
acceptanceCriteria: Not yet specified — needs data; the set of endorsement reasons is not known and the backend needs to define and supply the list
requirements.sourceNotes: 2026-09-17 transcript: user selects an endorsement reason from a collection of values; needs data, backend needs to provide the list. New functionality — no archive coverage; existing backend systems may need to support the field at all.

requirements.fr: Users can trust that the endorsement reasons offered are correct for the policy's state and effective date
acceptanceCriteria: Not yet specified — needs data; whether endorsement reasons are state-specific or effective-dated is unknown
requirements.sourceNotes: 2026-09-17 transcript: are endorsement reasons state-specific? Are they effective-dated, or can they change at any time?

requirements.fr: Users can optionally record a case number, cross-checked against Salesforce
acceptanceCriteria: Not yet specified — case number is optional on initiation; whether and how it validates against a Salesforce case is undefined pending scope (TBD)
requirements.sourceNotes: 2026-09-17 transcript: case number is optional; validated against Salesforce cases — write as AC/FR but attach a TBD flag, scope unknown and new functionality. FR-LC-01 AC1 covers capturing a case number; Salesforce validation is new beyond that.

requirements.fr: Users can add a requester, and notify more than one person of the endorsement
acceptanceCriteria: Not yet specified — new functionality; adding a requester is believed to let a user attach multiple people to be notified about the endorsement, broader than a single requester-email field
requirements.sourceNotes: 2026-09-17 transcript: user can add a requester; lets you attach multiple users to be notified with the endorsement; believed to be new functionality not currently supported. FR-LC-01 AC5 (a single requester email, with an open CC-field question) is the closest existing coverage.

requirements.fr: Users can add free-text details describing what the endorsement is doing
acceptanceCriteria: A free-text field for additional endorsement details is available on initiation
requirements.sourceNotes: 2026-09-17 transcript: user can enter additional endorsement details explaining what's happening. FR-LC-01 AC1 (notes).

requirements.fr: Users can quickly select an important date when setting the endorsement's effective date
acceptanceCriteria: Users can select from the policy's important dates — inception, previous endorsement effective dates, and (pending the cancellation-date open question) the cancellation date — rather than only entering a date manually
requirements.sourceNotes: 2026-09-17 transcript: date picker should let users quickly select previous endorsement dates; consolidated into a single AC covering policy inception, previous endorsements, possibly the cancellation date. No archive coverage of a quick-select date control.

requirements.fr: Users see a bounded, meaningful set of previous endorsement dates in the quick-select, not every endorsement ever issued
acceptanceCriteria: Not yet specified — what counts as "most recent," and whether there is a limit on how many dates are offered, are both undefined
requirements.sourceNotes: 2026-09-17 transcript: find out if there's a limit on how many dates are offered; show the most recent endorsement(s), not every single one — needs a definition of most recent.

requirements.fr: Users can see key policy facts on the create-endorsement form without leaving it
acceptanceCriteria: Policy cost, business name, policy number and policy term are each shown on the form — confirm "policy cost" is the intended field, since the source recording of this item was unclear
requirements.sourceNotes: 2026-09-17 transcript: the create endorsement form displays policy cost, business name, policy number, and policy term (transcript audio garbled on the first item — noted for confirmation, not assumed).

requirements.fr: Users can clear the changes they have made on the form
acceptanceCriteria: A clear action discards the form's current entries
requirements.sourceNotes: 2026-09-17 transcript: users can clear the changes on the form.

requirements.fr: Users can save an endorsement in its current, unpublished state and resume it later
acceptanceCriteria: An in-progress endorsement — its initiation fields and any edits made inside it — can be saved without publishing
A saved draft can be reopened and continued from where it was left
New functionality; more detail on what "current state" must capture, and where a saved draft is surfaced for resuming, is pending
requirements.sourceNotes: 2026-09-17 transcript: save draft — save an endorsement in its current state and resume later; new functionality flag, more details to come. This is the journey's core new capability, called out as its own requirement set distinct from initiation, because it has no precedent in the current platform at all — today an edit applies immediately or not at all.

requirements.fr: Navigating away from an in-progress endorsement does not silently discard it
acceptanceCriteria: The user is warned, or the endorsement is saved as a draft automatically, before an in-progress endorsement is lost to navigation
requirements.sourceNotes: FR-LC-04 AC3. Today navigating away tears the endorsement down — the gap saving-as-draft is meant to close, but the two are not automatically the same behavior.

requirements.fr: Users can abandon an endorsement deliberately, and cannot lose one by accident
acceptanceCriteria: Cancelling an endorsement asks for confirmation before discarding work
Cancelling is unavailable while a rerate or publish is in flight
requirements.sourceNotes: FR-LC-04 AC1–AC2. Not directly raised in the 2026-09-17 review; carried forward as the counterpart to the save-draft FR above — together they are what "decide as a unit whether to publish or discard" (this journey's user story) requires.

decisionsCarriedForward: This container holds one undifferentiated form, not one form per class (confirmed 2026-09-17). Once an endorsement is opened, Policy change and Servicing update edits across every domain this container holds are entered in the same session with no screen-level split by class. What submitting the form triggers per class — full rerate/publish always, or something lighter for non-rated-only submissions — is open.
This journey is net-new capability, not a re-specification of existing behavior — estimates should treat it as greenfield, per the index.
The endorsement binds to the coverage period containing the chosen effective date, and the user is warned if that differs from the period they were reading (FR-LC-01 AC2–AC3).
technicalNotes: Removed 2026-09-17 (open questions, per review): "What counts as a 'most recent' endorsement date for the quick-select, and is there a cap on how many are offered?" — duplicates the 'not yet specified' criterion already carried on the bounded-date-list FR itself.
openQuestions: What set of endorsement reasons exists, and are they state-specific or effective-dated? Needs data; blocks the endorsement-reason FR entirely.
Does case-number validation against Salesforce belong in this phase at all? Explicitly flagged TBD.
What does "requester" actually mean now — one email, or a list of people to notify? This session's description is broader than the archive's single requester-email field.
Can a cancelled policy be endorsed effective beyond its cancellation date? Raised explicitly with no answer given.
Is "policy cost" the correct field name for the first item shown on the create-endorsement form? Source recording was unclear.
Does saving a draft double as the fix for the navigate-away data-loss problem (FR-LC-04 AC3), or are they two separate behaviors?
Do abandoned drafts appear in the audit trail? Carried unchanged from the index's own open question 1 on this journey.

Is a pending draft visible from the read journeys it touches? Carried unchanged from the index's own open question 2 — the policy-cost/business-name/policy-number/policy-term display on the endorsement form is a small piece of evidence toward yes but does not settle it.
Concurrency: can two open drafts exist against the same coverage period? Carried unchanged from the index's own open question 3.

What does rerate/publish do with a transaction that only touched non-rated fields? Now that the shared-form decision is confirmed, an endorsement can be opened, edited and submitted touching nothing but a mailing address or a policy contact. Whether that still runs the full rerate-and-publish path or takes a lighter commit path is unanswered, and it's the same question Business Entity Data — Write and Servicing & Relationships — Write both raise.
